properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued August 29 at 5:24AM EDT until August 29 at 6:30AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

At 524 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts
were located along a line extending from 8 nm west of Mexico Beach to
16 nm east of Port St. Joe to 8 nm northeast of Apalachicola to St
George Island, moving east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats. Expect wind
gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours. Make sure
all on board are wearing life jackets.

Locations impacted include...
S Tower and O Tower.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 29 at 2:02AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
At 158 AM PDT, Doppler radar was tracking a cluster of strong
thunderstorms 9 miles southwest of Schellbourne, moving northeast at
45 mph. These cells have a history of producing cloud to ground
lightning strikes and could pass very close to the Kearny fire.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Cloud to ground lightning will pose a
risk to firefighters on the Kearny fire.

Locations impacted include...
Kearny fire, Lages Junction, Schellbourne, and Cherry Creek.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.
properties.area: White Pine County; South Central Elko County

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 29 at 4:54AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
At 454 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from near Eastpoint to 7 miles southeast of
Carrabelle. Movement was northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Carrabelle, Carrabelle Beach, Morgan Place, Saint Teresa, Turkey
Point, Royal Bluff, Mcintyre, High Bluff, Yent Place, Lanark Village,
St George Island St Pk, and Green Point.
properties.instruction:
Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.
properties.area: Inland Franklin; Coastal Franklin; Coastal Wakulla; Southern Liberty

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 29 at 4:32AM EDT until August 29 at 7:30AM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Montgomery County and northwestern Moore County in
central North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 730 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 432 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Troy, Carthage, Biscoe, Robbins, Star, Candor, Eagle Springs,
Steeds, Seven Lakes and Highfalls.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 29 at 4:14AM EDT until August 29 at 7:15AM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
At 414 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
2.5 and 4.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will
continue, but no additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marietta, Kennesaw, Acworth, Powder Springs, Austell, Fair Oaks,
Lithia Springs, Due West, Jim R Miller Park, Lost Mountain Park,
Kennesaw State University and Mableton.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Clark Creek, Chattahoochee River, Gothards Creek, Mud Creek,
Westbrook Creek, Noonday Creek, Dry Creek, Ward Creek, Etowah
River, Nickajack Creek, Noses Creek, Sweetwater Creek, Butternut
Creek, Rottenwood Creek and Powder Springs Creek.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Illinois River at Beardstown affecting Morgan, Cass, Brown and
Schuyler Counties.

.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil
moisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Illinois River at Beardstown.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 14.4 feet, Seepage problems begin in the Coal Creek
Drainage and Levee District.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM CDT Friday the stage was 14.4 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 PM CDT Friday was 15.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 11.4 feet Friday,
September 04.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the
latest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay tuned
for further updates on this flooding situation.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 900 AM CDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 28 at 8:36PM CDT until August 30 at 11:00AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Illinois...

Wabash River from Hutsonville to Vincennes.

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crested. Flooding should come to an end
on the Wabash over the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Seep water occurs behind levees on Indiana
side.  Hutson Creek begins to overflow from backwater.  Old Darwin
Road and a few rural roads in eastern Clark and Crawford counties
in Illinois are impassable.  Low agricultural land floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is no current observed data.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 6.4 feet Monday,
September 07.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.2
feet on 06/23/1946.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring. Most flood related deaths occur in
automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips, or
low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1015 AM CDT
/1115 AM EDT/.
properties.area: Crawford, IL; Lawrence, IL; Knox, IN; Sullivan, IN
